root.core_movement: From accepting oppression as inevitable to choosing freedom despite the cost

target_effect.audience: People trapped in situations they believe they cannot leave
target_effect.current_belief: Leaving is impossible or too dangerous; endurance is the only option
target_effect.desired_belief: Leaving is difficult but possible; staying has costs too

nodes.name: Protagonist Pattern
nodes.content: An entity that has accepted oppression as the price of survival
nodes.function: The ego consciousness identification point; embodies the audience's current state
nodes.children_hint: Could become: abuse survivor, colonized elder, employee in toxic workplace

nodes.name: The Accommodator
nodes.content: An elder who has spent decades advocating patience, whose caution is both wisdom and cowardice
nodes.function: Someone whose long history of accommodation makes the eventual choice more meaningful
nodes.resonance: The 'accepted oppression' becomes visible in decades of strategic surrender

nodes.name: Mira Castellan
nodes.content: Mira, 58, Kaelish council member. Lost her brother Daveth to the last rebellion 40 years ago. She encouraged him to join; she identified his body. Her caution is penance.
nodes.function: Specific person who embodies the accommodator archetype
nodes.resonance: Personal guilt over past failure + political role = visible stakes in every decision

nodes.name: Antagonist Pattern
nodes.content: A force that benefits from the protagonist's compliance and genuinely believes it's helping
nodes.function: Cannot be reasoned with because they see themselves as saviors

nodes.name: The Benevolent Colonizer
nodes.content: An empire that genuinely believes integration/assimilation saves the colonized from themselves
nodes.function: Makes leaving harder because the cage looks like protection
nodes.resonance: The 'believes it's helping' becomes 300 years of 'benevolent' rule

nodes.name: The Valdren Empire / Governor Aldric
nodes.content: A declining multi-ethnic empire, embodied in Governor Aldric who offers Mira a position because he truly believes integration is best for everyone
nodes.function: Specific face of the oppression; his sincerity makes him more dangerous than a tyrant
nodes.resonance: Empire becomes personal in Aldric's genuine offer of collaboration

nodes.name: Trap Pattern
nodes.content: A combination of practical constraints and psychological wounds that make leaving seem impossible
nodes.function: Explains why protagonist hasn't already made the change—must feel valid

nodes.name: Internal Trap
nodes.content: Guilt over past failure; belief that caution saves lives even if it costs souls
nodes.resonance: The psychological wound that makes the practical constraints feel insurmountable

nodes.name: Daveth's Death
nodes.content: Mira encouraged her brother to join the rebellion. Three weeks later she identified his body by his birthmark—his face was gone. She swore never again.
nodes.resonance: Guilt made specific: she told him it would work, and he believed her

nodes.name: External Trap
nodes.content: Economic dependence; historical trauma visible in the community
nodes.resonance: The practical reasons that reinforce the psychological wound

nodes.name: The Last Rebellion
nodes.content: 40 years ago: six hundred dead in three days. Kaelish trade routes run through imperial territory. Everyone remembers.
nodes.resonance: Not just Mira's wound—collective trauma that validates her caution

nodes.name: Catalyst Pattern
nodes.content: An event that attacks the next generation, making the slow death visible
nodes.function: The protagonist can endure harm to themselves; they cannot endure watching it come to those they protect

nodes.name: The Language Edict
nodes.content: Imperial law banning Kaelish in schools. Mira's grandson comes home crying, hand marked with a cane, asking: 'Grandmother, is our language bad?'
nodes.resonance: The attack on language is attack on existence; the child's question pierces her defenses

nodes.name: Ally Pattern
nodes.content: Someone who left before and survived—proof, not advocacy
nodes.function: Exists without pushing; their scars and freedom are both visible

nodes.name: Tomasz of Thrace
nodes.content: From a region that seceded 20 years ago. His people are poor but free. His left arm ends at the elbow. When he speaks his language in the market, he doesn't look over his shoulder.
nodes.resonance: Living proof requires no argument—his existence argues

nodes.name: Council of Patience
nodes.content: Council meeting on imperial taxes. Young members want protest. Mira counsels patience, wins the vote. Varen thanks her. She feels sick.
nodes.echo: Inverted at climax when she counsels the opposite

nodes.name: Teaching in Secret
nodes.content: Mira teaches grandchildren Kaelish words, songs, stories. Her grandson mispronounces a word; she corrects gently.

nodes.name: The Vote
nodes.content: Council chamber. Vote is tied. Mira stands, looks at firebrands, elders, emperor's portrait. She votes yes. Varen's face goes white. No going back.
nodes.function: The transformation moment; ego consciousness experiences the choice

nodes.name: The Response
nodes.content: Three weeks later. Four thousand soldiers at border. Two villages burned. Forty-three dead, including six children. Varen calls Mira a murderer. She does not disagree.
nodes.function: The choice has real, specific costs

nodes.name: The First Morning
nodes.content: Mira teaches her grandson Kaelish in the town square. Legally. He doesn't whisper. Neither does she. An old woman says 'Thank you.' Mira thinks of the six children. She will carry them forever.

metadata.user_input: I want women who are stuck in an abusive marriage to feel inspiration to walk away
